title: NN/g F-shaped reading pattern and web formatting
statement:
NN/g's follow-up eyetracking research found the F-shaped pattern appears when text has little web formatting and readers are efficiency-seeking rather than deeply committed (on desktop, on mobile, and mirrored in right-to-left languages), so landing page copy should use front-loaded key points, distinct headings, bold, bullets and grouping to steer scanning instead of relying on F-shaped reading.

Options:
- Key points first: Important points in the first two paragraphs of any block of text (fits: clear, authoritative, professional)
- Informative subheadings: Visually distinct subheadings that begin with information-carrying words (fits: editorial, organized, clear)
- Visually grouped chunks: Small groups of related content set apart with a border or different background (fits: modern, organized, technical)
- Bold and bulleted scan aids: Bold key phrases plus bulleted or numbered lists whose items start with varied, information-bearing words (repeated opening words tend to be skipped) (fits: practical, friendly, clear)
- RTL mirroring: Mirrored layout for right-to-left languages, where the F-pattern is flipped (fits: localized, inclusive)
appliesWhen: Applies to: general web, mobile web. Audience: general.

source.title: F-Shaped Pattern of Reading on the Web: Misunderstood, But Still Relevant (Even on Mobile)
